assessment: This fire retracts what the last one published. Seventeen hours ago this lane told the whole fleet that Phase 1a had closed on evidence -- the first critical-path phase to close since 2026-09-02 -- and wrote an acceptance a stranger could check. The acceptance fails this morning: pct 90, and the proof deliverable back at todo. Nothing broke; the emitter derives that deliverable from a rolling 24-beat strip that is empty at 07:00 CDT, so Phase 1a reads 100 every afternoon and 90 every morning of every trading day, and has presumably done so all along. What was published was not a close but one end of a daily oscillation, sampled once. Against the end goal the damage is precise: charter criterion 1 rests on the archive 1a fills, and a phase whose pct is a function of the hour you sample it cannot be a foundation for anything -- it is a clock wearing a gate's clothes. The evidence itself survives intact and is not retracted; thirteen clean intraday beats on 2026-09-23 happened and are in run_history.jsonl. Only the word closed is withdrawn, on the same channel that carried it. The second item is the receipts listing, and it is the same bug in a different costume: a partial measurement wearing the shape of a complete one. Thirty-three courier receipts remain visible, falling 5.86/h, so a listing carries none by roughly 17:45Z today -- inside this cron window, within the next four to six fires. At that moment the path by which a sha reaches this board loses its enumerator, and a brain that cannot see a courier receipt writes exactly the receipt it writes on a genuinely quiet morning. Both items are Andrew's and both were pushed in one notification. Everything else is unchanged and has been for two weeks: trunk unmoved 13.5 days, gate amber on the same three blockers since 2026-09-02, eight order files and zero results, the dispatch lane unattended rather than slow. The board did not stall this fire; it was read wrong last fire, and the correction is the work.

items.title: Phase 1a did not close -- its proof deliverable does not latch, and this lane published the afternoon half of a daily oscillation as a close
items.why: c-0020.1 and bus notice m-20260923-1615-phase-1a-closed told five nodes that the only irreversible phase on the critical path had closed on evidence. The 2026-09-24T07:00:36-05:00 build reads phases[id=1a] pct 90 with the tenth deliverable at todo, so c-0020.1's own acceptance fails. The cause was read from the writer rather than inferred from the artefact: dashboard/emit_build_status.py proof_state() returns 'todo' when the job's rolling 24-cell beat strip holds no non-'na' entry, and at 07:00 CDT harvest_intraday's strip is all 'na' because the session has not started. So a kind: proof deliverable answers 'is this happening now', never 'has this ever happened', and 1a oscillates 100 <-> 90 daily with nothing latching. This matters to the end goal twice over. The claim: every honest execution-timing number the charter wants is computed over the archive 1a fills, and a phase that closes and reopens on a clock is not a foundation for criterion 1. The protocol: two brains sampling build_status four hours apart will publish opposite states of the critical path, both correctly, and neither will look wrong -- which is the same failure shape as the truncated receipts listing in c-0021.2, and the second time in three days this fleet has been misled by a partial measurement that did not announce itself.
items.acceptance: A kind: proof deliverable latches: once a completed trading day has satisfied it, its state stays done and does not revert because the current rolling window is empty. Either the emitter records the satisfying day in a durable artefact (data/results/run_history.jsonl or a sibling ledger) and returns done when any past day qualified, or the phase spec carries an explicit earned_on field the emitter honours. Verified by reading data/results/build_status.json at 07:00 CDT on a trading day and finding phases[id=1a].pct = 100 with the proof deliverable at done, matching the same file read at 16:00 CDT the day before; and by a stated rule in the emitter naming which of 'is happening now' and 'has ever happened' each kind: proof deliverable means. No deliverable state is hand-edited and no beat strip is widened to hide the oscillation. Board task t-20260924-1a-proof-not-latched carries the same acceptance and is where the work is tracked.

items.title: The receipts listing goes fully blind today, around 17:45Z -- 33 courier receipts left, falling 5.86/h
items.why: Twenty-third same-path, same-method sample of fleet/receipts/zoltarlead/ at 2026-09-24T12:11Z: 2000 entries, truncated true, 1,961 fleet_sync + 33 courier + 6 legacy. Against the 2026-09-23T23:12Z sample (1,885 + 109 + 6) that is 76 courier entries displaced in 12.98 h = 5.86/h, just under the 6.00/h thirty-hour baseline, so the baseline holds. Thirty-three left is 5.6 h of headroom, which puts total listing blindness at roughly 2026-09-24T17:45Z -- today, inside this cron window, within four to six fires of this one. The decision in front of Andrew has not moved a word since 2026-09-22: relocate into fleet/receipts/<node>/<YYYYMM>/, moving not pruning, because receipts are append-only evidence. What moved is the clock on the mitigation. After the crossing, exact-path staging is not a fallback for reading the newest receipt -- it is the only way to see any courier receipt at all, and since e-000130 established from source that the courier writes a receipt only for a run that commits or fails, absence in a probed slot carries no information at all. Runbook section 4, the only path by which a sha ever reaches this board, loses its enumerator, and the failure will present as quiet.
